I’ve rewritten the project and it’s in tsp-rewrite.tar.gz (92 files), but none of the C# has been compiled or run. The .NET SDK and NuGet downloads are blocked in this sandbox. I checked every API I used against the library source code (System.CommandLine 2.0.14, xunit.v3 4.0.2, Reqnroll 3.3.4), and a separate review pass found nothing that should break the build. Your first time bash scripts/ci.sh is still the real test. If it fails, paste the output and I’ll fix it.

What did run here: ShellCheck passes on every script, the YAML is valid, and ci.sh and export.sh ran end to end with a fake dotnet stand-in.

Apply
bash
cd ~/src/dotnet/tsp
git rm -r --quiet TSP.sln Dockerfile .dockerignore \
  TravelingSalesman.ConsoleApp TravelingSalesman.Core TravelingSalesman.Specs TravelingSalesman.Tests \
  .github/workflows/build.yml docs/build.txt docs/results.html \
  scripts/PowerShell.txt scripts/bash.txt scripts/cat.ps1 scripts/push.ps1 \
  scripts/linux-installation-command.txt scripts/install-linux.sh scripts/install-kusl-tsp-simple.sh
rm -rf TravelingSalesman.ConsoleApp TravelingSalesman.Core TravelingSalesman.Specs TravelingSalesman.Tests
tar -xzf ~/Downloads/tsp-rewrite.tar.gz -C .
git add -A
time bash scripts/ci.sh
The rm -rf clears leftover build folders that git rm doesn’t touch. The new projects live under src/ and tests/, so it’s safe. LICENSE.txt and docs/llm/vendor/ are unchanged and not in the tarball.

What changed
Build setup: tsp.slnx replaces TSP.sln. global.json uses the .NET 10 SDK and opts dotnet test into Microsoft Testing Platform. All builds now go to artifacts/, and warnings are errors.
Packages: xunit.v3 4.0.2, Reqnroll.xunit.v3 3.3.4, System.CommandLine 2.0.14 and Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage 18.12.0. Serilog, coverlet and the old test runner packages are gone.
Core library: it has no dependencies now. Each solver sits behind one interface and is registered in a single catalog, so adding an algorithm doesn’t touch any command. Fixed seeds now give the same result every run. The three improving algorithms start from the Nearest Neighbor route, so they can never return anything longer than it.
The app: the interactive menu (which used Console.ReadKey and broke CI) is replaced by commands: tsp solve, tsp benchmark, tsp algorithms, plus --help and --version. The binary is called tsp and is built as a single Native AOT executable.
Tests: about 90 unit tests, including tests that run the app in-process, and 15 Reqnroll scenarios. Coverage reports go to artifacts/test-results.
Container: Containerfile uses mcr.microsoft.com/... image names and a minimal non-root runtime image. container.sh uses Podman if installed, otherwise Docker.
Scripts: no execute bit is needed anywhere. bash scripts/ci.sh runs lint, build, test, a smoke test of the app, a default benchmark, the AOT publish, the container build and the export to docs/llm/dump.txt. Use --skip-publish, --skip-container, --skip-export or --clean to change that. The publish step is skipped automatically if clang isn’t installed, and the container step if neither Podman nor Docker is.
GitHub Actions: both workflows only call the scripts, using the latest major versions (checkout v7, setup-dotnet v6, upload-artifact v7, download-artifact v8, action-gh-release v3). Release builds now cover linux-arm64 too, and attach a SHA256SUMS file. I also added dependabot.yml.
Things to know
The old install command will stop working. The command your servers use downloads scripts/install-kusl-tsp-simple.sh, which is deleted. The replacement is scripts/install.sh. It checks the download against the checksums file and installs to /opt/kusl-tsp/tsp, keeping the kusl-tsp command name.
Release file names changed to tsp-<platform>, with no commit hash, so releases/latest/download/... links stay stable.
The sample benchmark output in the README is illustrative. I couldn’t run the app, so replace it with real output once you have it.
Not confirmed: Reqnroll 3.3.4 doesn’t officially say it supports xunit.v3 4.x. Its source only uses parts of xunit that 4.0.2 still has, and I pinned the related xunit packages to 4.0.2. Test-running the scenarios is the real check.
On Fedora, the publish step needs sudo dnf install clang zlib-devel.
